rules.rationale: Halogen substitution adds hydrophobic surface and polarizability, the classic medchem driver of higher logD.
Extended aromatic pi systems give nonpolar surface that partitions into octanol favorably.
High heteroatom density raises hydrogen-bonding and desolvation cost, suppressing measured partition coefficient.
Source rotatable-bond role transferred strongly (0.758); flexible polar branches often add hydration without adding nonpolar surface.

skills.hypothesis: Retains the previously best-performing family: lipophilicity tracks nonpolar surface from halogens and aromatic rings, penalized by heteroatom density. Fails if halogen_high (98 candidates) is too sparse to inform the surrogate.

rules.rationale: Source smiles_long lowered solubility -11.46; logD opposes logS, so larger scaffolds should raise lipophilicity.
Source smiles_short raised solubility +6.89; small compact molecules are generally less lipophilic.
Maps the source H-bond donor role; fewer polar atoms means weaker hydration and higher partition coefficient.
Source ring role carried the strongest transfer weight (0.758); ring-rich scaffolds favor octanol partitioning.

skills.hypothesis: Transfer-saturated counter-hypothesis: length (confidence 0.224) and ring roles carry the ESOL signal with reversed sign. Fails if size effects are saturated and polar-group placement, not bulk, sets lipophilicity.

state.lesson: Across eight development seeds the hydrophobic-surface skill beat sign-reversed solubility transfer on both mean AUC (89.04 vs 85.73) and mean final best (91.42 vs 88.61), so the low-confidence, low-transfer-weight length relation (0.224 confidence, 0.040 prior weight) remains the weaker basis; the gap is suggestive, not causal, given the small seed set.
state.revision_summary: Kept the deployed halogen/aromatic/heteroatom family and replaced the extreme-length rule with a branch/rotatable-bond penalty, since the source rotatable-bond role transferred at 0.758 versus 0.224 for length. The second skill retains the sign-reversed ESOL transfer scaffold as an explicit counter-hypothesis, with confidence lowered and semantic mass slightly decayed. Deployment stays with the counter-hypothesis skill family, frozen before held-out evaluation.
